text: Every morning in winter, the rangers at Scaffold Peaks pin a notice to the board outside the ranger station. Hundreds of walkers pass the board on their way to the two tracks that lead to the summit. Most of them barely slow down. They glance at the first line of the notice, nod, and keep walking, already thinking about the view at the top. Last night, a metre of fresh snow fell on the eastern slopes, and strong winds piled it into unstable drifts above the east track. Ranger Okoye spent the early hours checking the slopes with a long metal probe, and she did not like what she found. The east track will stay closed until the snow settles. The west track, which is sheltered by a long rocky ridge, is still safe, although it is steeper and takes an extra hour. Last winter, a notice that began with a long weather report was ignored by almost everyone, and two walkers had to be rescued from a drift by a team on snowshoes. Ranger Okoye knows the one thing every walker must take away from the notice, even if they read only a few words: the east track is closed. She picks up her marker and starts writing.
